title: Divide et Calibra: Multiclass Local Calibration via Vector Quantization
claim: Calibration maps are built by quantizing representations into regions and composing shared parameters, with a partition picture showing the induced regions.
layout: 2 panels; left pipeline flows left-to-right with two colored paths, right Voronoi plot
description: The left panel (a) is a toy-example pipeline diagram. An input photo of a beluga whale goes through a frozen encoder E(x), giving z. A projection Φ(z) produces a segmented vector that is matched against a 4-entry codebook C. Two paths follow, each drawn in its own color. The green calibration path uses the VQ assignment indices s(1..3) to select calibration parameters A, B and σ², which combine into the Dirichlet concentration α, then feed f_cal. The orange prediction path sends the quantized vector q̄ through f_VQ into f_cal. A legend marks the paths, and snowflake and flame icons mark frozen and learnable parts. The right panel (b) shows a 2-D Voronoi tessellation with numbered centroids, scattered colored points, and regions shaded blue, orange and green.
caption: We depict our pipeline ([ref]) and Voronoi assignment procedure ([ref]).
abstract: Accurate and well-calibrated Machine Learning (ML) models are mandatory in high-stakes settings, yet effective multiclass calibration remains challenging: global approaches assume calibration errors are homogeneous across the latent space, while local methods often rely on representation-space dimensionality reduction, discarding latent directions relevant to miscalibration. To address these issues, we propose a compositional approach to multiclass calibration, where region-specific calibration maps are constructed from shared factors. We instantiate this idea via Vector Quantization (VQ), which induces a structured partition of the representation space, and an indexed parameterization of Dirichlet concentrations that enables parameter sharing across regions. Our approach learns heterogeneous calibration maps that generalize well even to sparse regions of the latent space. Experiments on benchmark datasets show significant improvements in local calibration while maintaining competitive global calibration and predictive performance.
